clue.text: Dull-sounding seaside area

indicators.note: the word sounding tells us to say the dull word out loud and hear another

parts.note: literal means prosaic and unimaginative, so dull

explanation.surface: A drab-sounding stretch of coast, the sort of resort no one raves about.
explanation.definitionFit: A littoral is the shore zone of a sea or lake, so a coastal region.

clue.text: Rebukes minor partners about nothing

indicators.note: about here means placed around, so the minor partners go round nothing

parts.note: minor means smaller, less
N and S, North and South, are partners at the bridge table
O, the round zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: Someone tells off junior colleagues in a firm for having no purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, North and South play as a partnership, a convention worth knowing; 'about' puts the round zero between the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Lessons in the sense of reproofs or punishments are rebukes, as in teaching someone a lesson.

clue.text: Flier heads away from Sw?

parts.note: someone heading away from south-west must swing round from facing south to facing north-east, and that instruction spelt out gives the bird

explanation.surface: A bird flies off in the direction opposite the south-west.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the whole as an instruction: face round from S (south) to NE (north-east). Turn + S + to + NE spells the shore bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The turnstone is a wading bird, and any bird is a flier.

clue.text: Behave like glutton — before tucking into eggs, finish off toast

indicators.note: tucking into means going inside, so the word for before goes into the eggs

parts.note: ova is the Latin plural for eggs
ere is a poetic word for before

indicators.note: finish off points to the final letter of toast

explanation.surface: A greedy eater wolfs eggs and then finishes off the toast.
explanation.definitionFit: To overeat is to eat too much, the defining habit of a glutton.

clue.text: Car signal bringing prompt assistance

parts.note: auto is short for automobile, a car
a cue is a signal to act or speak

explanation.surface: A car's indicator gives a timely warning to other drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: An autocue is a screen that feeds lines to a presenter, helping by prompting them.

clue.text: One way to travel from Louisiana via Texas

indicators.note: from tells us the letters are taken out of the run of words Louisiana via Texas

explanation.surface: A route for a journey that starts in Louisiana and passes through Texas.
explanation.definitionFit: To aviate is to fly an aircraft, which is a method of making a journey.

clue.text: Craftsmanship I obstruct in plant

parts.note: art means skill or craftsmanship
to choke a pipe is to block or obstruct it

explanation.surface: A craftsman confesses to clogging the workings of a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: The globe artichoke is a thistle-like vegetable plant.

clue.text: Batting first, Test is under control

indicators.note: first says the batting word comes ahead of the test word

parts.note: in cricket the side batting is said to be in
to check is to test

explanation.surface: A cricket side batting first in a Test match has the game well managed.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket: the batting side is 'in'; a Test is an international match.
explanation.definitionFit: Held in check means restrained, kept under control.

clue.text: Left-winger runs to kick left-half

parts.note: trots means runs at a gentle pace

indicators.note: left-half means the first, left-hand half of the word kick

explanation.surface: A football left-half sprints forward to take a kick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left-half' is a football position in the surface; here it takes the left half (KI) of 'kick'. The revolutionary is usually spelt Trotsky.
explanation.definitionFit: Leon Trotsky was a Marxist revolutionary, a figure of the political far left.

clue.text: Show international player's trial on film

parts.note: to screen a film is to show it
a Test is an international cricket or rugby match

explanation.surface: A televised international match gives a sportsman a chance to prove himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A screen test is a filmed audition for an actor, a player in the theatrical sense.

clue.text: Explorer brings business to satisfactory conclusion

explanation.surface: A famous explorer is also a shrewd dealer who seals the deal.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain James Cook charted the Pacific; to cook a deal informally is to settle or manage it successfully.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Cook was an eighteenth-century navigator and explorer; cooking something up means arranging it to a desired end.

clue.text: They feed on the shore, like Walrus and Carpenter

explanation.surface: Lewis Carroll's pair of shellfish eaters are likened to wading birds.
explanation.walkthrough: In Lewis Carroll's poem the Walrus and the Carpenter lure young oysters along the beach and eat them all.
explanation.definitionFit: These black-and-white waders eat shellfish on beaches; Carroll's two characters literally catch the shellfish to eat.

clue.text: Pen that is provided for terrier

parts.note: a pen stands for a writer, here Sir Walter Scott, the novelist
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: An enclosure has been laid on for a small dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' looks like an enclosure for an animal, but it stands for a writer, Walter Scott.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottie is the familiar short name for a Scottish terrier breed of dog.

clue.text: One who succeeds in female's new trio

parts.note: taken as written
her is the possessive for a female

indicators.note: new tells us the letters of trio are made into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone triumphs as part of a woman's newly formed group of three.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges TRIO into ITOR.
explanation.definitionFit: One who succeeds to property or a title is an heir, someone who takes on a legacy.

clue.text: Cooked kipper, duck and meat in pastry

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are mixed up and transformed

parts.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket, a zero

explanation.surface: A menu offers cooked kipper, duck and a meat pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooked' rearranges KIPPER plus O (duck: a cricketer's score of nought).
explanation.definitionFit: A pork pie is a raised pie of chopped pork in a hot-water crust.

clue.text: Scattered in 500 pieces, it may put paid to slugs

indicators.note: scattered tells us the letters are spread out and rearranged

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

explanation.surface: Pellets scattered all over the garden in hundreds should finish off the slugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scattered' mixes up D (Roman 500), PIECES and IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A pesticide is a chemical poison for pests, so it can kill garden slugs.

clue.text: French crew assembled ship's cargo

parts.note: an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: A French crew gathered to load a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: A rowing eight is a crew of eight oarsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Freight is goods carried by a vessel, its load.

clue.text: Strike episode produces angry behaviour

parts.note: to ram is to strike hard
a page in history is an episode or chapter

explanation.surface: A walkout incident leads to fury on the picket line.
explanation.definitionFit: A rampage is a spell of violent, uncontrolled conduct.

clue.text: Perceptible understanding

explanation.walkthrough: Split as 'in sight' it means visible; whole, it means deep perception.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in sight can be seen; insight is an intuitive grasp of something.

clue.text: Money paid initially is returned in store

indicators.note: in signals that one piece goes inside the store word

parts.note: a depot is a storehouse

indicators.note: returned means the word is is read backwards

explanation.surface: Cash handed over at the start is given back in the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Money' alone could be the definition, but 'paid initially' belongs with it: a deposit is the first payment, not a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A deposit is a down payment made at the outset of a purchase.

clue.text: No longer in employment, Captain Corcoran's verbal standards aren't maintained

definitions.text: Captain Corcoran's verbal standards aren't maintained

explanation.surface: A retired captain lets his old standard of polite speech slip.
explanation.walkthrough: In Gilbert and Sullivan's HMS Pinafore, Captain Corcoran claims he never uses a big, big D (damn); read as 'D is used', the answer means he lapses.
explanation.definitionFit: Disused means no longer put to work; split, it says the swear word D is now being uttered.

clue.text: Repair I bungled, that's plain

indicators.note: bungled means messed up, so the letters of repair and I are jumbled

explanation.surface: A botched repair job turns out simple and obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie is a wide expanse of flat grassland, a plain.

clue.text: Man one has to beat on the touchline?

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them
a gent is a man

explanation.surface: A football manager feels he must thrash a player standing on the touchline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touchline' is the edge of a sports pitch, but a tangent is a line that touches a curve.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangent is a straight line touching a curve at a single point.

clue.text: Smart in Latin, so it's altogether odd to produce this

definitions.text: Smart in Latin, so it's altogether odd to produce this

indicators.note: altogether odd says the whole run of smart in Latin so must be put in a strange new order

explanation.surface: A clever classicist warns that a garbled rendering of Latin is the result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'altogether odd' jumbles SMART, IN, LATIN and SO; a garbled rendering from Latin is just what the clue describes.
explanation.definitionFit: A mistranslation is an incorrect rendering of text from one language into another.

clue.text: Hit a square cut? Absolutely!

explanation.surface: A batsman's square cut is praised as a perfect shot.
explanation.walkthrough: A square cut is a cricket stroke in the surface; here it is a hairstyle cut straight across the forehead, and 'bang on' or 'bang right' means exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: To bang is to strike; a bang is a straight-cut fringe; bang as an adverb means precisely.

clue.text: Person who rallies before failing in China

parts.note: to rally someone is to tease or banter with them, so one who rallies is a teaser
a vice is a moral failing

explanation.surface: A tennis player who keeps rallying collapses in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country, but it is porcelain crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea service is a matched set of crockery, often porcelain.

clue.text: Bullyboy?

parts.note: split as a bully and a boy's name, this describes someone who blusters and intimidates and is also a man's first name

explanation.walkthrough: To hector is to bully, and Hector was a Trojan hero, here also a boy's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Hector as a noun is a blustering intimidator, and it is also a forename.

clue.text: This disciple had gone off before Matthew, Mark etc

indicators.note: gone off means turned bad, so the letters of had are rearranged

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
the Gospels of Matthew and Mark are books of the New Testament, NT

explanation.surface: A follower had left before the evangelists arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone off' rearranges HAD into ADH.
explanation.definitionFit: An adherent is a follower or supporter of a cause or leader.
